column5: Excuse my lack of enthusiasm, Damek.\nI think there are more pressing matters at hand.\nWe still need to decide what to do with {i}him{/i}.
column6: 恕我提不起兴致，达梅克。\n我认为眼下有更紧迫的事要处理。\n我们还得决定该怎么处置{i}他{/i}。

column5: He tilts his head toward \"Salus\", who shakes his own head in return.
column6: 他朝“萨卢斯”偏了偏头，对方则摇了摇头作为回应。

column5: We require no maintenance.\nWe simply wish to fight, and teach.\nOur legacy demands to be passed on.
column6: 我们无需照料。\n我们只求战斗，并传道授业。\n我们的传承需要延续下去。

column5: There you have it.\nI don't think there's anything we can do.\nHe won't be of any harm to us, right?
column6: 你也看到了。\n我觉得我们无能为力。\n他不会伤害我们的，对吧？

column5: That's what we thought about the Honor Guard.\nAre you really going to gamble on the spirits again?\nWhat if there's a chance he's just lying to us, Damek?
column6: 当初我们对荣誉卫队也是这么想的。\n你真打算再拿灵赌一次吗？\n万一他只是在骗我们呢，达梅克？

column5: We have no reason to lie.\nAnd we do not appreciate this accusation.\nUsing the Honor Guard, we fortified these tunnels.
column6: 我们没有理由撒谎。\n而且我们不喜欢这种指控。\n我们借助荣誉卫队，加固了这些隧道。

column5: It is thanks to us that you survived this ordeal.\nMany of our citizens were sacrificed in order to do this.\nControlling The Triumvirate's forces was taxing, to say the least.
column6: 你们能在这场劫难中幸存，全靠我们。\n为此，我们牺牲了许多同胞。\n控制三人执政团的军队，至少可以说是极耗心力。

column5: Then why did they kill almost all of us during the attack?
column6: 那袭击时他们为什么几乎把我们杀光了？

column5: Our control was strong — but not strong enough.\nIt was easy for The Grand Inquisitor to overpower us.\nUntil today, he had never set foot in these tunnels.
column6: 我们的控制很强——但还不够强。\n大审判官轻易就压制了我们。\n在今天之前，他从未踏足这些隧道。

column5: We do not mind answering questions.\nBut we {i}do{/i} mind being accused of wrongdoing.\nEverything we've done — we've done to help your cause.
column6: 我们不介意回答问题。\n但我们{i}确实{/i}介意被指控做了坏事。\n我们所做的一切——都是为了帮助你们的事业。

column5: To what end?
column6: 目的何在？

column5: The Triumvirate's end.
column6: 终结三人执政团。

column5: Ulric concedes, simply shaking his head.{w}\nIt seems there was a counter to all of his objections.
column6: 乌尔里克让步了，只是摇了摇头。{w}\n看来他所有的质疑都被一一驳倒了。

column5: I think we should trust him, Ulric.\nHe's answered so many of our questions.\nThings make more sense now, wouldn't you say?
column6: 我觉得我们该相信他，乌尔里克。\n他回答了这么多问题。\n现在事情清楚多了，你不觉得吗？

column5: He doesn't respond.{w}\nHowever, Fortaime steps forward.
column6: 他没有回应。{w}\n不过，福泰姆上前一步。

column5: What should we call him, though?
column6: 不过，我们该怎么称呼他？

column5: We do not require a name.
column6: 我们不需要名字。

column5: You might think that, but you still need one.\nIt's out of convenience, not necessity.
column6: 你也许这么想，但你还是需要一个。\n这是为了方便，而非必需。

column5: Convenience?
column6: 方便？

column5: Yeah. Nobody really {i}needs{/i} a name.\nIt just helps us talk to one another, you know?\nIt's especially helpful in battle, or while strategizing.
column6: 对。其实没人{i}需要{/i}名字。\n它只是方便我们彼此交流，你懂吧？\n在战斗中，或者制定策略时，尤其有用。

column5: Very well. We will think of a name.
column6: 好吧。我们会想个名字。

column5: However, before much time passes, Valessa interjects.
column6: 然而，没过多久，瓦莱莎插话了。

column5: Howl.
column6: 豪尔。

column5: Hmm?
column6: 嗯？

column5: That's what Damek said, right?\n\"Driven by the howls of countless spirits\".\nIt seems fitting, given the circumstances.
column6: 达梅克是这么说的，对吧？\n“被无数灵的嚎哭所驱使”。\n结合眼下的情形，这名字似乎很贴切。

column5: Valessa, I—
column6: 瓦莱莎，我——

column5: We accept this moniker.\nHowever, we must discuss another matter.\nThis strategizing you speak of. We wish to help.
column6: 我们接受这个名号。\n不过，我们必须讨论另一件事。\n你所说的制定策略。我们想帮忙。

column5: That's my job, actually.
column6: 其实，那是我的工作。

column5: And look where it got you.
column6: 看看它把你带到了什么地步。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: Your blind faith in spirits caused all of this.\nOur judgment will not be clouded. We wish to take your place.\nRemember, you are no longer in charge. This is the King's choice.
column6: 你对灵的盲目信仰导致了这一切。\n我们的判断不会受蒙蔽。我们想取代你。\n记住，你已不再掌权。这是国王的选择。

column5: Your blind faith in spirits caused all of this.\nOur judgment will not be clouded. We wish to take your place.\nRemember, you are no longer in charge. This is the Queen's choice.
column6: 你对灵的盲目信仰导致了这一切。\n我们的判断不会受蒙蔽。我们想取代你。\n记住，你已不再掌权。这是女王的选择。

column5: Howl turns to face me.
column6: 豪尔转身面对我。

column5: We wish to be your advisor, Monarch.\nWe've watched this world for almost an eternity.\nWe know how the enemy works, and thinks.
column6: 我们想成为您的顾问，君主。\n我们已守望这个世界近乎永恒。\n我们了解敌人如何行事、如何思考。

column5: It would be the wisest course of action.\nDamek is responsible for this catastrophe.\nHe would be unfit to give you advice in the future.
column6: 这将是明智的做法。\n这场灾难是达梅克的责任。\n今后他不适合再向您进言。

column5: That is absolutely untrue!\nIn this world, we learn from our mistakes, Howl.\nWe don't condemn others based on bad decisions.
column6: 这绝对不实！\n在这个世界，我们是从错误中学习的，豪尔。\n我们不会因为别人做了糟糕的决定就否定他。

column5: Perhaps that is why you are easily oppressed.\nThere is no room for error in these final days.\nPerhaps in the future you can atone for this.
column6: 也许正因如此，你们才轻易被压迫。\n在这最后的日子里，容不下任何差错。\n也许将来你能为此赎罪。

column5: I can tell that they're about to get locked in a heated argument.{w}\nTo avoid this, I slam my hands down on the war table, startling them.{w}\nA loud echo reverberates through the room as I assert my authority.
column6: 我看得出他们即将陷入激烈的争吵。{w}\n为了避免这一幕，我双手猛拍作战桌，把他们吓了一跳。{w}\n一声巨响在房间里回荡，我借此确立了自己的权威。

column5: Hmm...?
I let them know that I want Damek to be my advisor.{w}\nI agree with everything he'd said, and I still don't really know Howl.{w}\nBeing an advisor required both knowledge {i}and{/i} teamwork.
column6: 我让他们知道我属意达梅克做我的顾问。{w}\n他说的每一点我都赞同，而我对豪尔仍算不上了解。{w}\n做顾问既需要知识，{i}也{/i}需要团队精神。

column5: Very well.
column6: 好吧。

column5: Thank you.
column6: 谢谢你。

column5: They still stared at each other with evil eyes.{w}\nI could tell that animosity was growing between them.{w}\nHowever, this was neither the time or the place for that.
column6: 他们仍恶狠狠地盯着彼此。{w}\n我看得出他们之间的敌意在滋长。{w}\n然而，此时此地都不是计较这些的时候。

column5: We appreciate the opportunity.
column6: 我们感谢这个机会。

column5: Really...?
column6: 真的……？

column5: Damek looks crushed, and defeated.{w}\nBut all I did was make the best choice I could.{w}\nIt's something I'd need to get used to in my new position.
column6: 达梅克看上去深受打击，一败涂地。{w}\n但我只是做出了当时能做出的最佳选择。{w}\n这是我身居新位必须习惯的事。

column5: However, Damek still needed to serve The Rebellion.{w}\nSupressing his emotions, he focused on his duty.{w}\nWhile we were busy at the idol, he formulated a plan.
column6: 不过，达梅克仍需要为反抗军效力。{w}\n他压下情绪，专注于自己的职责。{w}\n当我们在灵像那儿忙碌时，他已经拟定了一个计划。

column5: Those matters aside, we still need to make our next move.\nThere's an upcoming ball in Alarinthia. It's held annually.\nThe palace is open for a few days only. We can go.
column6: 那些事暂且不提，我们还得决定下一步行动。\n阿拉林西亚即将举办一场舞会，每年一次。\n王宫只开放几天。我们可以去。

column5: It's likely that Vivien will make a move against Draycu.\nIf she does, we can use that as an opportunity to form an alliance.\nIf she doesn't, then we can seek out an audience with Draycu.
column6: 薇薇安很可能会对德雷库有所动作。\n如果她动手，我们可以借此机会结盟。\n如果她不动，我们就设法求见德雷库。

column5: Either side would have a wealth of forces to offer.\nWe need their aid if we're going to win the final battle.\nI'll get the boats ready. We can leave tomorrow morning.
column6: 无论哪一方，都能提供大量兵力。\n要想赢下最终决战，我们需要他们的援助。\n我会备好船只。我们明早就能出发。

column5: I'm sure Alex will be able to give us a capable ship.\nIf we're going to make this ball, we need the best of the best.\nShips were part of our terms, so I'm sure he'll be able to comply.
column6: 我相信亚历克斯能给我们一艘像样的船。\n要赶上这场舞会，我们需要最好的船。\n船只是条约的一部分，所以我相信他会照办。

column5: I'm sure Nada will be able to give us a capable ship.\nIf we're going to make this ball, we need the best of the best.\nShips were part of our terms, so I'm sure she'll be able to comply.
column6: 我相信娜达能给我们一艘像样的船。\n要赶上这场舞会，我们需要最好的船。\n船只是条约的一部分，所以我相信她会照办。

column5: He gathers up some papers, and starts to walk away.
column6: 他收起一些文件，转身离开。

column5: Meet back here in the morning. All of you.\nWe can go over any last minute stuff before we leave.\nThe rest, we'll have plenty of time to discuss on the voyage.
column6: 明早在这里集合。所有人。\n出发前我们可以再过一遍最后的细节。\n其余的，航行途中我们有充足的时间讨论。

column5: We all nod at one another before leaving the room.{w}\nI'm thankful that I'd be able to get some sleep — however little.{w}\nI make my way back to my room, constantly checking my back.
column6: 我们互相点头，随后离开房间。{w}\n我很庆幸自己能睡上一会儿——哪怕很短。{w}\n我朝自己的房间走去，一路不停回头张望。

column5: They'd never catch us off guard again.{w}\nNext time we fought — it would be their end.
column6: 他们再也别想打我们个措手不及。{w}\n下次交锋——就是他们的终结。

column5: Howl has now permanently joined your party.
column6: 豪尔现已永久加入你的队伍。

column5: I enter my room and let out a loud sigh. I can finally relax.{w}\nAs short as my rest would be, it was better than no rest at all.{w}\nI notice I was followed, but I expected as much after what happened.
column6: 我走进房间，长舒一口气。终于能放松了。{w}\n哪怕休息很短，也总比没有强。{w}\n我注意到有人跟了过来，但经历了那些事，我早有预料。

column5: It was Damek.
column6: 是达梅克。

column5: He approaches slowly, and acts nervous.{w}\nAt least he doesn't appear angry with me.
column6: 他缓缓走近，举止紧张。{w}\n至少他看起来没有生我的气。

column5: Look, I just wanted to say — no hard feelings.\nIf anything, I'm angry with Howl. He was rude.\nBlaming everything on me? That's not right.
column6: 听着，我只是想说——别往心里去。\n要说生气，我气的是豪尔。他太无礼了。\n把一切都怪到我头上？那不对。

column5: There's no way that this was all my fault.\nWe were tricked, and there was no way to counter it.\nWe weren't in any position to doubt what the spirits showed us.
column6: 这不可能全是我的错。\n我们被算计了，而且根本无从招架。\n我们当时没有立场去怀疑灵向我们展示的东西。

column5: But now? Everything is different.\nI guess I'll take a step back for the time being.\nMaybe this is a blessing in disguise, you know?
column6: 但现在呢？一切都不同了。\n我想我暂时会退后一步。\n也许这是因祸得福，你懂吗？

column5: I'll get to relax, and spend time with the crew.\nI honestly can't remember the last time I got to unwind.\nHopefully Howl is able to strategize as well as he lets on.
column6: 我可以放松一下，和船员们相处。\n说实话，我都记不清上次放松是什么时候了。\n但愿豪尔的谋略真如他所表现得那么好。

column5: But all of those spirits inside of him...?\nI wouldn't be surprised if they could outsmart me.\nI'm curious though — do you think he can induce visions?
column6: 但他体内那么多灵……？\n就算他们比我聪明，我也不会意外。\n不过我很好奇——你觉得他能引出幻象吗？

column5: I shrug, unsure of how to answer.{w}\nHowever, that would be a useful tool.
column6: 我耸耸肩，不知该如何作答。{w}\n不过，那会是个很有用的手段。

column5: I'm still confused about all of this.\nHe said that visions were a part of his culture, right?\nBut they didn't see The Triumvirate coming. Not at all.
column6: 我对这一切仍然困惑。\n他说过幻象是他文化的一部分，对吧？\n可他们没能预见三人执政团的到来。完全没有。

column5: Just {i}what{/i} are they...? Where did they come from?\nAre there other worlds out there that have fallen victim to this?\nIf there are — then what chance do {i}we{/i} stand?
column6: 他们{i}究竟{/i}是什么……？他们从何而来？\n外面还有其他世界也沦为了他们的猎物吗？\n如果有——那{i}我们{/i}又有什么胜算？

column5: It's true. The implications of this truth were staggering.{w}\nHowever, we had something that nobody else would.{w}\nI take the blade off my back, and rest it against the wall.
column6: 没错。这个真相的意味令人震惊。{w}\n然而，我们拥有别人不会有的东西。{w}\n我把背上的刃取下，靠在墙边。

column5: I guess that blade really {i}is{/i} our only hope.\nLook — I'll let you sleep. I know how interruptions can be.\nI just wanted to let you know that I don't hate you. I never will.
column6: 看来那把刃{i}真的{/i}是我们唯一的希望。\n听着——我不打扰你休息了。我知道被打断是什么滋味。\n我只是想让你知道，我不恨你。永远不会。

column5: Whether I'm your strategist or not, you're still our savior.\nBesides, I could never speak out of turn. You're royalty now.\nJust make sure to be responsible with your influence, Monarch.
column6: 无论我是不是你的战略家，你依然是我们的救世主。\n再说，我绝不会越礼妄言。你现在是皇族了。\n只是务必善用你的影响力，君主。

column5: He gives me a slight bow, as a sign of respect, before leaving.{w}\nI'm not sure what happened — but he seemed different now.{w}\nI guess the events that happened today would change any man.
column6: 他微微躬身，以示敬意，然后离开。{w}\n我不确定发生了什么——但他现在似乎不一样了。{w}\n我想今天发生的事，换作谁都会有所改变。

column5: It was Howl.
column6: 是豪尔。

column5: He approaches slowly, with resolve in his steps.{w}\nHowever, he doesn't seem angry in any way.{w}\nThat was good, since I sided with Damek.
column6: 他缓缓走近，步伐坚定。{w}\n不过，他看上去丝毫没有怒气。{w}\n这很好，毕竟我站在了达梅克这边。

column5: We must express displeasure at your decision.\nDamek made a mistake, and remains unpunished.\nThe lives that were lost {i}beg{/i} for justice. We are that justice.
column6: 我们必须对你的决定表示不满。\n达梅克犯了错，却依然未受惩罚。\n逝去的生命{i}渴求{/i}正义。我们就是那正义。

column5: Damek was only believing in the spirits, like we all do.{w}\nNow that we know the truth, he will approach things differently.{w}\nHe would never intentionally lead us into danger. He's honorable.
column6: 达梅克只是像我们所有人一样信仰灵。{w}\n既然我们知道了真相，他会用不同的方式处事。{w}\n他绝不会刻意把我们引入险境。他是个正直的人。

column5: Honor?
column6: 正直？

column5: He crosses his arms, unimpressed.
column6: 他双臂交叉，不为所动。

column5: Honor is a term used to stay the hand in difficult situations, [firstname].\nWhen the final drop of blood must be spilled, and your {i}honor{/i} stops you?\nWhat then? Is the future of our world on the shoulders of those so weak?
column6: “正直”是危急时刻用来收手的托词，[firstname]。\n当最后一滴血必须流下，而你的{i}正直{/i}却让你停手？\n那又当如何？我们世界的未来要托付给如此软弱之人吗？

column5: He scoffs.
column6: 他嗤笑一声。

column5: Do not concern yourself with honor. \nThe enemy does not, and this is why they win.\nConcern yourself with the correct actions — not the right ones.
column6: 不必为正直费心。 \n敌人不会，所以他们才赢。\n你要在意的是正确的行动——而非正当的行动。

column5: That is all the advice we have for you today, [firstname].\nBut we do not trust Damek to make the right decisions in the future.\nThe fact that he left the Honor Guard alive is proof of that. He hesitates.
column6: 这就是我们今天能给你的全部建议，[firstname]。\n但我们不信任达梅克今后能做出正确的决定。\n他留了荣誉卫队活口，就是明证。他会犹豫。

column5: This hesitation will not go away simply because he knows what we are.\nThe truth of the \"Spirit Realm\" does not change strategy on the war table.\nWith that said, we will leave you be. Ruminate on this in the future, my King.
column6: 这种犹豫不会因为他知道了我们是什么就消失。\n“灵界”的真相并不会改变作战桌上的策略。\n话已至此，我们不打扰了。日后请细想，我的国王。

column5: This hesitation will not go away simply because he knows what we are.\nThe truth of the \"Spirit Realm\" does not change strategy on the war table.\nWith that said, we will leave you be. Ruminate on this in the future, my Queen.
column6: 这种犹豫不会因为他知道了我们是什么就消失。\n“灵界”的真相并不会改变作战桌上的策略。\n话已至此，我们不打扰了。日后请细想，我的女王。

column5: He gives me a slight bow, as a sign of respect, before leaving.{w}\nBeing the Exodus wielder was intense enough, but being the Monarch?{w}\nThankfully I had the support of my friends. They would keep me strong.
column6: 他微微躬身，以示敬意，然后离开。{w}\n光是流亡之刃的持有者已经够让人紧绷了，更别说当君主？{w}\n幸好有朋友们的支持。他们会让我保持坚强。

column5: I lay down in bed, and it isn't much longer before I drift off to sleep.{w}\nWhen I wake up, rested and refreshed, I head to the War Room.{w}\nEveryone is there, as expected. It's time to get things moving.
column6: 我躺上床，没过多久便沉沉睡去。{w}\n醒来时，我精神饱满，径直前往作战室。{w}\n所有人都如约在场。是时候推动事情了。

column5: Howl approaches the war table, and rests his hands upon it.{w}\nBefore speaking, he moves pieces of wood around the war table.{w}\nThey represent different things. He rests The Rebellion's piece over Alarinthia.
column6: 豪尔走近作战桌，双手按在桌上。{w}\n开口之前，他在作战桌上挪动几块木牌。{w}\n它们各有含义。他把反抗军的木牌放在阿拉林西亚上。

column5: We sail for Alarinthia, to forge an alliance.\nHowever, the nature of that alliance remains to be seen.\nIt will be with either the insurgent Vivien, or the ruler Draycu.
column6: 我们扬帆前往阿拉林西亚，缔结同盟。\n不过，同盟的对象尚未确定。\n要么是叛军薇薇安，要么是统治者德雷库。

column5: We will meet with both under the guise of a ball.\nHeld annually, it is a celebration of Draycu's power and influence.\nIt is also the perfect chance for Vivien to make a move, or challenge him.
column6: 我们将借舞会之名与两人会面。\n这场舞会每年举办，是彰显德雷库权势与影响力的庆典。\n也是薇薇安动手或向他发起挑战的绝佳时机。

column5: Both parties will be present, so we will see what both can offer.\nOur goal is Alarinthian allies to aid our final assault on Balteus.\nDamek worked with our pirate allies to secure transport.
column6: 双方都会到场，所以我们能看看他们各自能提供什么。\n我们的目标是争取阿拉林西亚的盟友，协助我们对巴尔泰乌斯的最终进攻。\n达梅克已与我们的海盗盟友接洽，安排好了船只。

column5: We meet at the docks after we're done talking here.\nIt will be a skeleton crew, to avoid arousing suspicion.\nThere should be enough beds for all of us to sleep.
column6: 这里谈完后，我们在码头集合。\n为免引人怀疑，只留最基本的船员。\n床位应该够我们所有人休息。

column5: The voyage will end at this time tomorrow.\nEnough food and drink will be packed for all of us.\nBring your essentials. We will provide everything else.
column6: 航程将于明天此时结束。\n会为我们所有人备足食物和饮水。\n带上你的必需品。其余一切由我们提供。

column5: Are there any objections?
column6: 有异议吗？

column5: He glances over at Ulric, who returns a piercing gaze.
column6: 他瞥了乌尔里克一眼，后者回以锐利的目光。

column5: Except for that one.
column6: 除了那位。

column5: Ulric shrugs, and the meeting continues.
column6: 乌尔里克耸耸肩，会议继续进行。

column5: Damek approaches the war table, fiddling with the wooden figures resting ontop of it.{w}\nThey represent different things. The figure for the Rebellion, he places on Alarinthia.{w}\nOur next objective was clear. We'd be sailing to the far east to secure an alliance.
column6: 达梅克走近作战桌，摆弄着桌上的木制棋子。{w}\n它们各有含义。他把代表反抗军的棋子放在阿拉林西亚上。{w}\n我们的下一个目标很明确。我们将航向远东，争取同盟。

column5: Each year, Draycu holds a ball. Essentially, it's to show off his power.\nIt's open to the public, which means Vivien will likely make a move.\nI'd say it's either an assassination attempt, or a tournament request.
column6: 德雷库每年都会举办一场舞会。本质上是为了炫耀他的权势。\n舞会向公众开放，这意味着薇薇安很可能会有所动作。\n我猜要么是行刺，要么是提出比武挑战。

column5: During the ball, we will meet with both of them.\nOur goal is to secure an Alarinthian army to help us out.\nIf we do this, our chance of success will increase tenfold.
column6: 舞会期间，我们将与两人会面。\n我们的目标是争取一支阿拉林西亚军队来相助。\n若能办成，我们成功的几率将提升十倍。

column5: Each party, if they're willing, will likely request something in return.\nIt may be impossible to avoid being caught up in Alarinthian politics.\nIf it comes to anything extreme, we will have Ulric help us out.
column6: 各方若愿意合作，多半都会提出条件作为回报。\n恐怕难免会被卷入阿拉林西亚的政治漩涡。\n若事情发展到极端，我们会让乌尔里克出面相助。

column5: I trust there are no objections?
column6: 我想没有异议吧？

column5: Nobody raises a concern, but I can tell that Ulric is upset.
column6: 没人提出异议，但我看得出乌尔里克很不高兴。

column5: We will set sail immediately after this meeting.\nI've already arranged transportation with our Pirate allies.\nIt's a twenty-four hour voyage, so pack your essentials.
column6: 会议结束后我们立刻启航。\n我已和海盗盟友安排好了船只。\n航程二十四小时，所以带好必需品。

column5: Food and drink have already been pre-packed.\nNone of us should go hungry or thirsty during the trip.\nAnd there are enough beds for all of us to sleep, too.
column6: 食物和饮水已经提前备好。\n旅途中我们谁都不该挨饿受渴。\n而且床位也够我们所有人休息。

column5: The voyage will be a nice time to get some relaxation in.\nHowever, once we get to Alarinthia, we have to be serious.\nOur success directly affects our odds of surviving this war.
column6: 航程是个放松的好时机。\n不过，一到阿拉林西亚，我们就必须严肃起来。\n我们的成败直接关系到能否在这场战争中活下来。

column5: We've ensured that our comrades received a proper burial.\nThey're resting with the spirit idol, and we'll close off that passage.\nFor their sake, please leave it undisturbed. They deserve rest.
column6: 我们已经让战友们得到妥善安葬。\n他们安息在灵像旁，我们会封死那条通道。\n看在他们份上，请勿打扰。他们应当安息。

column5: He inspects a piece of paper in his hand before continuing.
column6: 他看了看手里的一张纸，然后继续。

column5: The volunteers from Valinorth are starting to have visions.\nThey will accompany us to Alarinthia, and help our cause.\nThankfully, there were no side effects, or losses.
column6: 来自瓦利诺斯的志愿者开始出现幻象。\n他们会随我们前往阿拉林西亚，协助我们的事业。\n幸好没有副作用，也没有伤亡。

column5: We have our army of Seers, [firstname].\nHopefully you'll get to meet them soon.
column6: 我们有了一支先知军队，[firstname]。\n希望你能尽快见到他们。

column5: However, the bodies you imbued with power have started to move.\nThey will accompany us to Alarinthia, and help our cause.\nThankfully, they accepted this fate. There is no confusion.
column6: 不过，你注入力量的那些躯壳开始行动了。\n他们会随我们前往阿拉林西亚，协助我们的事业。\n幸好他们接受了这个命运。没有混乱。

column5: We have our army of Vessels, [firstname].\nHopefully you'll get to meet them soon.
column6: 我们有了一支容器军队，[firstname]。\n希望你能尽快见到他们。

column5: With all of that said, I think it's time to end this meeting.\nAre there any questions before we head to the shipyard?\nRemember, once we leave, we may not be back for a while.
column6: 说了这么多，我想该结束这次会议了。\n去造船厂之前还有什么问题吗？\n记住，我们一旦离开，可能很久都不会回来。

column5: Fortaime steps forward.
column6: 福泰姆上前一步。

column5: What exactly happens at this ball?
column6: 这场舞会到底会发生什么？

column5: I'm not sure. Dancing and feasting, I'd imagine.\nDraycu wants to pamper everybody he can. That's his goal.\nIf his people are happy, then there's less fighting over the throne.
column6: 我不确定。我想，无非是跳舞和宴饮。\n德雷库想尽可能笼络所有人。这就是他的目的。\n子民开心，对王位的争夺就会少些。

column5: So basically one big party, then.
column6: 所以基本上就是一场盛大的派对。

column5: Correct.
column6: 没错。

column5: Awesome. The last party we were ever going to have was cancelled.\nLet's say we finally have your induction ceremony, eh, [firstname]?\nExcept now it's not for being a Seer. It's for being a {i}King{/i}.
column6: 太好了。我们原本最后的派对泡汤了。\n不如说，你的就任典礼终于补上了，是吧，[firstname]？\n只不过现在不是成为先知，而是成为{i}国王{/i}。

column5: Awesome. The last party we were ever going to have was cancelled.\nLet's say we finally have your induction ceremony, eh, [firstname]?\nExcept now it's not for being a Seer. It's for being a {i}Queen{/i}.
column6: 太好了。我们原本最后的派对泡汤了。\n不如说，你的就任典礼终于补上了，是吧，[firstname]？\n只不过现在不是成为先知，而是成为{i}女王{/i}。

column5: We all nod at each other. It's true, my last ceremony was cancelled.{w}\nIt {i}was{/i} Draycu's party, but we could celebrate for our own reasons.
column6: 我们互相点头。的确，我上一次的典礼被取消了。{w}\n那{i}确实{/i}是德雷库的派对，但我们可以为自己而庆祝。

column5: Just — try not to draw attention to yourselves, alright?\nIt may be a party, but Alarinthia's fate will change behind the scenes.\nRemember why we're there, and don't lose sight of our original goal.
column6: 只是——尽量别引人注目，好吗？\n它或许是场派对，但阿拉林西亚的命运将在幕后改变。\n记住我们为什么去，别忘记最初的目标。

column5: Of course.
column6: 当然。

column5: Fortaime steps back, satisfied.
column6: 福泰姆满意地退后一步。

column5: Why didn't Vivien make a move at any of the other parties?\nI guess I mean to ask — what makes this year special?\nWhat if we go there, and she ends up doing nothing?
column6: 薇薇安为什么没在往年的任何一场舞会上动手？\n我想问的是——今年有什么特别？\n万一我们去了，她却什么都不做呢？

column5: That is when we focus only on Draycu.\nNo matter what happens, we have options.\nIt is wise to plan for roads you may not even take.
column6: 那时我们就只专注于德雷库。\n无论发生什么，我们都有选择。\n为未必会走的路做准备，是明智之举。

column5: If that happens, then we focus on Draycu.\nAt the end of the day, we'll still have an option.\nWe're just planning for many possible scenarios.
column6: 如果那样，我们就专注于德雷库。\n归根结底，我们仍有选择。\n我们只是在为各种可能的情形做打算。

column5: Alright.
column6: 好吧。

column5: Valessa nods, her curiosity sated.{w}\nThere's a brief silence, and no further questions.
column6: 瓦莱莎点点头，好奇心得到了满足。{w}\n短暂的沉默后，再无其他问题。

column5: Very well. Dismissed.\nLet's pack our things and meet at the docks.\nWe'll set sail in three hours, so don't be late.
column6: 很好。解散。\n大家收拾行装，在码头集合。\n三小时后启航，别迟到。

column5: Very well. Meeting dismissed.\nYou have three hours to pack and get to the docks.\nOur goal is important, so we {i}will{/i} leave you behind.
column6: 好。会议到此为止。\n你们有三小时收拾东西并赶到码头。\n我们的目标至关重要，所以{i}一定{/i}会把迟到的人留下。

column5: With that said, almost everybody rushes out of the room.{w}\nExcept for Howl. He stays behind, and eyes me down.{w}\nBefore I get ready to leave, I ask him what he wants.
column6: 话音刚落，几乎所有人都冲出了房间。{w}\n唯独豪尔留了下来，盯着我看。{w}\n在我准备离开前，我问他有何事。

column5: We've been given a room in the Crew Quarters.\nPlease stop by and see us before you leave.\nIt is important for us to learn more about you.
column6: 我们在船员舱分到了一个房间。\n出发前请来见我们一面。\n多了解你，对我们很重要。

column5: He bows at me before leaving.
column6: 他向我鞠了一躬，然后离开。

column5: Until then, your highness.
column6: 那么，回头见，陛下。

column5: He was definitely taking this Monarch thing seriously.{w}\nBut given his culture, and the power within me, it makes sense.{w}\nI take one last look at the War Table before heading out.
column6: 他显然把“君主”这回事看得很重。{w}\n但考虑到他的文化，以及我体内的力量，这也说得通。{w}\n出门前，我最后看了一眼作战桌。

column5: The War Table is used to track your relationships with each character.{w}\nThe amount of hearts indicates how many Heart-to-Hearts you have completed.{w}\nWhen a character's heart gauge reaches four, you can click them to access a special scene.
column6: 作战桌用于追踪你与每位角色的关系。{w}\n心形数量代表你已完成多少次交心。{w}\n当某位角色的心形计量达到四颗，点击他们即可进入一场特殊剧情。

column5: These scenes are required to earn each character's loyalty.{w}\nThe loyalty of your followers affects both Morale, and their fate.{w}\nDo not neglect Heart-to-Heart conversations, or these special \"Loyalty Scenes\".
column6: 这些剧情是赢得每位角色忠诚的必要条件。{w}\n追随者的忠诚会影响士气，也影响他们的命运。{w}\n不要忽视交心对话，以及这些特殊的“忠诚剧情”。

column6: 当你准备启程前往阿拉林西亚时，回到马泽奥码头。{w}\n造船厂前方船只旁会显示一个新的地图图标。

column5: Valessa leads me through Mazeo, to some sort of hidden cove area.{w}\nThere's a large ship, and it looks like some sort of dock, with no signs of life.{w}\nStashes of treasure lay about, and it's apparent that this place has been abandoned.
column6: 瓦莱莎带我穿过马泽奥，来到一处隐秘的湾洞。{w}\n那里停着一艘大船，看起来像是个码头，却毫无生机。{w}\n四处堆放着成堆的财宝，显然这里早已被废弃。

column5: After we returned, I got talking to the pirates.\nYou know, to pick up any information on our parents.\nIt turns out, this is their base of operations. Their HQ.
column6: 我们回来之后，我和那些海盗聊了聊。\n你知道，是想打听父母的消息。\n结果发现，这里就是他们的行动基地。他们的总部。

column5: Kinda funny, isn't it? We both ended up having HQ's in Mazeo.\nBut to be honest, that's where I'd like the similarities to end.\nThe more I learn about them — the more I {i}hate{/i} them...
column6: 挺讽刺的，不是吗？我们俩最后都在马泽奥有了总部。\n但说实话，我希望相似之处到此为止。\n我越了解他们——就越是{i}恨{/i}他们……

column5: They kept running off to Mazeo, and left us in Salus' hands.\nNow that I think about it, he raised us more than they ever did.\nI guess they were more interested in this life of piracy. It's awful.
column6: 他们总是跑回马泽奥，把我们丢给萨卢斯照看。\n现在想想，他才是把我们养大的人，远比他们用心。\n我想他们更在意的，是这种海盗生涯。真恶心。

column5: She looks around the cove, taking in the environment.
column6: 她环顾湾洞，打量着四周的环境。

column5: I wanted to come here with you to face the truth.\nOur parents were bad people. There's no denying it.\nThey wanted {i}this{/i} to be their legacy, rather than us...
column6: 我想和你一起来这里面对真相。\n我们的父母是坏人。这一点无可否认。\n他们想让{i}这些{/i}成为他们的遗产，而不是我们……

column5: She starts to walk around the area, and I follow behind her.
column6: 她开始在这一带走动，我跟在她身后。

column5: Look at all this junk they valued more than us.\nWeapons, money, more money — and lame scrolls.\nMaps to some far-off treasure and riches, I'm sure.
column6: 看看这些他们看得比我们还重的破烂。\n武器、钱、更多的钱——还有无聊的卷轴。\n我敢肯定，是通往某处远方宝藏和财富的地图。

column5: Picking up a handful of coins, she throws them into the nearby water.
column6: 她抓起一把钱币，扔进旁边的水里。

column5: Sorry for going off like that. It just makes me really angry.\nWe idolized them for so long, thinking the world lost good people.\nBut to realize that maybe the world is better off without them? It's hard.
column6: 抱歉，我刚才失控了。这事就是让我很生气。\n我们崇拜了他们那么久，以为世界失去的是好人。\n可意识到也许没有他们世界会更好？这很难接受。

column5: Anyway, thanks for coming along with me.\nI just thought it would be good to do this together.\nI don't know how Fortaime would handle it, if I'm honest.
column6: 总之，谢谢你陪我一起来。\n我只是觉得，一起来会好一些。\n说实话，我不知道福泰姆能不能承受得住。

column5: She turns to face me, with a hint of a smile on her face.
column6: 她转身面对我，脸上带着一丝微笑。

column5: You know, I realized I'm different from all of these rebels.\nThey've been living oppressed, in the shadow of The Triumvirate.\nBut it was never The Triumvirate that held me back — it was always myself.
column6: 你知道，我意识到自己和这些反抗军都不一样。\n他们一直活在三人执政团的阴影下，受着压迫。\n但束缚我的从来都不是三人执政团——一直是我自己。

column5: I wanted to be a person who could make my parents proud.\nI wanted to do what society demanded of me. I wanted to be {i}perfect{/i}.\nBut this is a real wake up call. {i}Nobody{/i} is perfect. We're all flawed at heart.
column6: 我想成为一个能让父母骄傲的人。\n我想做社会要求我做的事。我想变得{i}完美{/i}。\n但这次真的把我敲醒了。{i}没有人{/i}是完美的。我们内心都有缺陷。

column5: To realize that, and embrace it? I think that's all I needed to do.\nI feel like now, I can be who I want — and not who other people want me to be.\nIt feels like such a small thing, but a different perspective can change a lot, you know?
column6: 明白这一点，并接纳它？我想这就是我需要做的全部。\n我觉得现在，我可以做我想做的人——而不是别人希望我成为的人。\n这听起来微不足道，但换个视角能改变很多，你懂吗？

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点点头。

column5: Well then, want to take a look around?\nIf we can find anything to help us in Balteus, then it's not a total loss.\nI'm sure there's something around here that we can take along with us.
column6: 那么，想四处看看吗？\n如果能找到什么在巴尔泰乌斯派得上用场的东西，就不算白来。\n我相信这附近总有我们能带走的东西。

column5: She starts rummaging through various crates and sacks.{w}\nI do the same as her, but find nothing of note — except money.{w}\nIt could help after the war, but right now we needed something more.
column6: 她开始翻找各种箱子和麻袋。{w}\n我也跟着翻，却一无所获——除了钱。{w}\n战后或许用得上，但眼下我们需要的是别的东西。

column5: Hey, look what I found!
column6: 嘿，看我发现了什么！

column5: She pulls out a pair of daggers, and starts inspecting them.
column6: 她掏出一对匕首，仔细端详。

column5: I think I remember these. \nBack when I was a kid, I swear I saw them.\nThat means they must've belonged to my parents.
column6: 我想我记得这些。 \n我还是孩子的时候，发誓见过它们。\n那说明它们一定属于我的父母。

column5: Or my Mother, to be exact.\nJust an intuition — so I can't say for sure.\nBut I'd be willing to bet that my hunch is correct.
column6: 准确地说，是我母亲。\n只是直觉——所以我不能确定。\n但我愿意打赌，我的预感没错。

column5: Did you find anything good, [firstname]?
column6: 你找到什么好东西了吗，[firstname]？

column5: I shake my head. There wasn't anything of note.{w}\nAside from those daggers, none of it was helpful.
column6: 我摇了摇头。没什么值得一提的。{w}\n除了那对匕首，其余都派不上用场。

column5: What do you say? Should I keep them...?\nMight come in handy when we attack Balteus.
column6: 你说呢？我该留下它们吗……？\n进攻巴尔泰乌斯时也许能派上用场。

column5: Well, that was a good question, actually.{w}\nShe came here to move on from her parents.{w}\nTaking their stuff could just be a constant reminder.
column6: 嗯，这问题其实问得好。{w}\n她来这里是为了放下父母。{w}\n带走他们的东西，也许只会时时勾起回忆。

column5: On the other hand, however, maybe she could make them her own.{w}\nIt was hard to tell whether or not this would help or hinder her in the future.{w}\nBut with our final battle almost upon us, I'm afraid that I couldn't afford a mistake.
column6: 但另一方面，也许她能让它们真正属于自己。{w}\n很难说这会在将来帮她还是拖累她。{w}\n可最终决战近在眼前，我怕自己承担不起一次失误。

column5: Make them my own, huh?\nI think I like the sound of that.
column6: 让它们属于我自己，是吗？\n我喜欢这说法。

column5: She puts the daggers in the leather straps on her back.{w}\nReturning with a smile, it seems like she's ready to head home.
column6: 她把匕首插进背后的皮带上。{w}\n她带着微笑走回来，似乎已经准备好回家了。

column5: You know what? You're right.\nThis is pretty much grave-robbing.
column6: 你知道吗？你说得对。\n这基本上就是盗墓。

column5: She places the daggers back where she found them.{w}\nTurning back to me with a smile, it seems like her visit is over.
column6: 她把匕首放回原处。{w}\n她转身朝我微笑，看来此行已经结束。

column5: Well, I guess now I need to focus on the important stuff.\nWhat kind of person do I want to be — after this war is over?\nI'm no longer held back by anything, so I guess my dreams are the limit.
column6: 好吧，我想现在我该专注于重要的事了。\n这场战争结束后——我想成为什么样的人？\n再也没有什么束缚我了，所以我想，梦想没有上限。

column5: She smiles, and blushes softly.
column6: 她微微一笑，脸颊泛起红晕。

column5: And as long as we're talking about dreams...
column6: 既然说到了梦想……

column5: Taking a step forward, she places her hands in mine.{w}\nI smile at her, and give them a soft squeeze, which she returns.
column6: 她上前一步，把双手放进我的手中。{w}\n我朝她微笑，轻轻握了握，她也回握。

column5: I never would've dreamed that we'd become this close.\nWe've gone through so much together, and become so strong.\nYou're part of the reason I was brave enough to face my past like this.
column6: 我从没想过我们会变得这么亲密。\n我们一起经历了那么多，变得如此坚强。\n我能鼓起勇气这样面对过去，你也是原因之一。

column5: But with my past taken care of, I'd like to look toward the future.\nAnd if there's one thing I want the most — it's for you to be a part of it.\nYou know, I keep thinking back to that dance we had. I felt so special.
column6: 但既然过去已经了结，我想展望未来。\n如果说我最想要的一样东西——那就是让你成为其中一部分。\n你知道，我总回想起我们共舞的那次。我感觉自己如此特别。

column5: There were so many eyes on us though, I felt kind of restricted.\nI mean, I wanted to kiss you — that's what you're supposed to do, right?\nAt the end of a dance, of course. I think it's tradition, or something like that.
column6: 可当时那么多双眼睛盯着我们，我有点放不开。\n我是说，我想吻你——本来就该这么做，对吧？\n当然，是在舞曲结束时。我想那是传统，或者类似的东西。

column5: It's just that—
column6: 只是——

column5: Before she can finish, I step forward, and slowly move my face toward hers.{w}\nI stop halfway, and wait for her to close the distance. Her face is bright red.{w}\nWhen our lips touch together, it feels as if the world has stopped moving.
column6: 她还没说完，我便上前一步，脸缓缓凑近她。{w}\n我在半途停住，等她缩短剩下的距离。她的脸涨得通红。{w}\n当我们的唇相触时，仿佛整个世界都静止了。

column5: This was our moment. Just for the two of us.
column6: 这是属于我们的时刻。只属于我们两人。

column5: I move my head back, but let my hands find their way to her sides.{w}\nShe stammers, and looks around the cove, clearly embarrassed and shy.
column6: 我把头稍稍后仰，双手却自然而然地落到她的腰侧。{w}\n她结结巴巴，环顾着湾洞，满脸羞涩。

column5: I guess that does it, then...\nAll this time, and I only had to ask.\nI'm glad to finally know how you feel, for sure.
column6: 那这事就这么定了……\n这么久以来，原来我只要开口就行。\n我很高兴终于确切地知道了你的心意。

column5: She takes a deep breath of relief, as if a massive weight was now gone.{w}\nI totally understand. This was a big deal for her — and for me, as well.
column6: 她如释重负地深吸一口气，仿佛卸下了千斤重担。{w}\n我完全理解。这对她意义重大——对我也是。

column5: Should we head back then...?\nI guess you have other things to tend to.\nTruth be told — I needed this. Thank you.
column6: 那我们该回去了吗……？\n你大概还有别的事要处理。\n说实话——我需要这趟行程。谢谢你。

column5: With that, we're on our way out of the cove.{w}\nShe faced her past in that moment, and came out ever stronger.{w}\nI have no doubt that she'd continue to grow into an amazing woman.
column6: 于是，我们踏上离开湾洞的路。{w}\n她在那一刻直面了过往，也变得更坚强。{w}\n我毫不怀疑，她会继续成长为一个了不起的女人。

column5: Before we leave for good, I turn back and look around once more.{w}\nThis was where our parents conducted most of their business...?{w}\nThat means this is the closest I've been to them in decades.
column6: 在彻底离开前，我回头又看了一眼。{w}\n这里就是父母做大部分生意的地方……？{w}\n也就是说，这是我几十年来离他们最近的一次。

column5: Goodbye...
column6: 再见了……

column5: Fortaime takes me back to Valinorth, and we look at The Grand Tree.{w}\nIt makes sense that he'd want to accomplish his lifelong dream before the final battle.{w}\nWith those metallic claws he'd found in Mazeo, I think he could finally achieve what he wanted.
column6: 福泰姆带我回到瓦利诺斯，我们望着巨树。{w}\n他想在最终决战前实现毕生的梦想，这很合理。{w}\n有了他在马泽奥找到的那些金属爪，我想他终于能得偿所愿了。

column5: And of course, he wanted me to achieve it with him.{w}\nI'm grateful that he chose me, but I'm also a little worried.{w}\nIs this really something I could pull off, even with those tools?
column6: 当然，他希望我和他一起完成。{w}\n我很感激他选择了我，但也有点担心。{w}\n就算有那些工具，这事我真能做到吗？

column5: Well, I guess this is it.\nI can't leave for Balteus with any regrets.\nSo I'm finally going to do it — I'll climb The Grand Tree.
column6: 好吧，我想就是现在了。\n我不能带着遗憾前往巴尔泰乌斯。\n所以我终于要动手了——我要爬上巨树。

column5: And with someone like you, no less.\nThink they'll talk about this in the history books?\nI mean, I don't think anybody else has done this before.
column6: 而且还是和你这样的人一起。\n你觉得历史书里会记载这件事吗？\n我是说，我觉得以前从没人做到过。

column5: We're going to be the first.
column6: 我们将是第一个。

column5: Here, you need to put these on like gloves.\nThere's another pair that goes on your feet as well.\nAfter that, we just climb. We don't need to find footholds.
column6: 来，你得把这些像手套一样戴上。\n还有一副是套在脚上的。\n之后，我们只管往上爬。不用找落脚点。

column5: Being able to create them ourselves? Now that's a good invention.\nI gotta give credit where credit is due. Mazeans know what they're doing.\nDon't tell anybody though — these might very well be under the trade ban.
column6: 能自己造出来？这才是好发明。\n该夸就得夸。马泽奥人确实有两下子。\n不过别跟别人说——这东西很可能在贸易禁令之列。

column5: He gives me a quick wink.{w}\nIt's alright though, I won't tell anybody.
column6: 他朝我飞快地眨了下眼。{w}\n不过没关系，我不会说出去的。

column5: It looks way taller than I remember.\nI'd try to give you some advice, but I don't have any.\nWith those tools, this should be pretty easy. At least, I hope.
column6: 它看起来比我记忆中高多了。\n我本想给你点建议，可我也没有。\n有这些工具，应该挺容易的。至少我希望如此。

column5: Just don't fall, [firstname].\nI don't know if you could survive something like that.\nI've fallen from way shorter trees and been in pain for months.
column6: 千万别摔下去，[firstname]。\n我不知道你摔下来还能不能活。\n我从矮得多的树上摔下来，都疼了好几个月。

column5: He sure is great at instilling confidence...
column6: 他可真是擅长给人打气……

column5: Well then — got everything ready?\nLet's find a good starting point, and do this.
column6: 那么——都准备好了吗？\n我们找个好的起点，开始吧。

column5: And don't forget that there's a kiss on the line!\nSo let's consider this a race. Are you ready...?
column6: 别忘了，赌注可是一个吻！\n那就把它当成一场比赛吧。你准备好了吗……？

column5: But remember it's a race, so no holding back...!\nI want to make sure that we both give it our all. No regrets.
column6: 但记住这是比赛，所以别留手……！\n我要确保我们都全力以赴。不留遗憾。

column5: He enters a stance that implies he's ready to begin.{w}\nI nod to let him know that I'm ready, and assume the same stance.{w}\nWe make our way to the base of The Grand Tree, and look up.
column6: 他摆出准备开始的架势。{w}\n我点头示意自己准备好了，也摆出同样的姿势。{w}\n我们走到巨树脚下，抬头仰望。

column5: This is the first time I realize how tall it actually is.{w}\nWould we really be able to make it to the top...?{w}\nA doubt wells up within me, but I don't voice it.
column6: 这是我第一次意识到它究竟有多高。{w}\n我们真能爬到顶端吗……？{w}\n一丝疑虑在心头涌起，但我没有说出口。

column5: I bet I'll be the first one there!
column6: 我赌我会第一个到顶！

column5: With that said, he digs his claws into the tree and starts to climb.{w}\nI watch him for a few moments before replicating his actions to a tee.{w}\nAfter a few minutes of doing this, we're extremely far from the surface.
column6: 说完，他把爪子扎进树干，开始攀爬。{w}\n我观察了他一会儿，然后分毫不差地照做。{w}\n这样爬了几分钟后，我们离地面已经极高。

column5: Scared of heights? Make sure not to look down!\nI for one, love the view. This is part of why I do it.
column6: 怕高吗？千万别看下面！\n我倒很喜欢这景色。这也是我这么做的原因之一。

column5: Hey, no fair! I was taking a breather...!\nDidn't think you'd be the type to play dirty!
column6: 嘿，不公平！我刚才只是在歇口气……！\n没想到你是会耍手段的那种人！

column5: He laughs we scale the tree at almost the same rate.{w}\nI can't imagine doing this without those claw-like tools.{w}\nIn fact, they make this pretty easy. There's no risk of falling.
column6: 他笑了，我们以几乎相同的速度攀爬。{w}\n我无法想象没有这些爪状工具该怎么做。{w}\n事实上，它们让攀爬变得相当轻松。完全没有坠落的风险。

column5: It allows me to take a step back and admire Fortaime's skill.{w}\nHe was climbing trees for his entire life without this kind of aid.{w}\nI suddenly appreciate his every stumble and fall — his every bruise.
column6: 这让我能腾出心思，欣赏福泰姆的技艺。{w}\n他这一辈子都在没有这种助力的情况下爬树。{w}\n我忽然懂得了他每一次踉跄跌倒——每一处淤青的分量。

column5: As we get higher and higher, we start to get enveloped in a canopy of leaves.{w}\nWe aren't quite high enough that they've become red, but it's still an impressive sight.{w}\nIt blocks us from seeing the village below us, but it's beautiful to look at, regardless.
column6: 我们越爬越高，渐渐被一片树冠包裹。{w}\n我们还没高到让叶子变红，但那景象依然壮观。{w}\n它遮住了下方的村庄，但无论怎样，看上去都很美。

column5: It really helps solidify just where we are. We're scaling The Grand Tree.{w}\nNobody has done this before, and it's been his dream for decades, now.{w}\nHowever, due to his challenge, the competitive spirit starts appearing within me.
column6: 这让我真切地意识到自己的所在。我们正在攀登巨树。{w}\n从没人做到过，而这已是他的梦想几十年了。{w}\n然而，因为他的挑战，我心中也升起了好胜心。

column5: At the rate we're going, I could very well beat him to the top.{w}\nIn fact, if it was a race — that would pretty much be the point.{w}\nBut this was still his dream, and he might deserve the moment.
column6: 照这个速度，我很可能比他先到顶。{w}\n事实上，既然是比赛——那不就是重点吗。{w}\n但这终究是他的梦想，也许这一时刻该属于他。

column5: I decide to intentionally throw my progress.{w}\nFortaime deserves to win. I feel like it's only fair.{w}\nAs we get higher, we reach the bloodleaves on high.
column6: 我决定故意放慢进度。{w}\n福泰姆应该赢。我觉得这样才公平。{w}\n随着我们越爬越高，我们到了高处的血叶层。

column5: When we reach the final stretch, I fake a small stumble.{w}\nNothing to put myself in danger, just enough to cause a slight delay.{w}\nAfter Fortaime has gotten far enough up, I get myself back on track.
column6: 到了最后一段，我假装踉跄了一下。{w}\n不会让自己陷入危险，只够造成一点延迟。{w}\n等福泰姆爬得足够远后，我才重新跟上。

column5: It's not much longer before we reach the top, but he's clearly victorious.{w}\nHe laughs as he sits on a massive branch. Big enough to support both our weight.{w}\nI follow him up there and sit beside him, taking a huge sigh of relief. We did it...!
column6: 没过多久我们就到了顶部，但他显然胜出。{w}\n他笑着坐到一根巨大的树枝上。大到足以承受我们两人的重量。{w}\n我跟着爬上去，坐到他身边，长长舒了口气。我们做到了……！

column5: I can't believe we did it, [firstname]...!\nAnd of course, I had a feeling that I'd win.\nNever think you can rise above the master!
column6: 真不敢相信我们做到了，[firstname]……！\n当然，我就感觉自己会赢。\n别以为你能超越师傅！

column5: I decide to fully commit to the idea of a race.{w}\nUsing all of my strength, I push myself as much as I can.{w}\nAs we get higher, we reach the bloodleaves near the top.
column6: 我决定全心投入这场比赛。{w}\n我用尽全力，拼命向上。{w}\n随着我们越爬越高，我们到了靠近顶端的血叶层。

column5: This is it...! The final stretch.{w}\nI use all of my effort, in an attempt to defeat Fortaime.{w}\nAnd soon enough — I do — we reach the top, and sit on a massive branch.
column6: 就是现在……！最后一段。{w}\n我拼尽全力，想击败福泰姆。{w}\n很快——我做到了——我们到达顶部，坐到一根巨大的树枝上。

column5: Wow, I can't believe we did it...!\nAnd actually — I can't believe you won!\nI guess you're just a natural at everything, huh?
column6: 哇，真不敢相信我们做到了……！\n而且——真不敢相信你赢了！\n看来你做什么都天生在行，是吧？

column5: He smiles, and inches a bit closer toward me as we sit on the branch.
column6: 他微笑着，坐在树枝上，一点点向我靠过来。

column5: Look at that view...\nI know we can't see the village, but these leaves...?\nI never thought I'd get to see them up close like this before.
column6: 看看那景色……\n我知道我们看不到村庄，但这些叶子……？\n我从没想过有生之年能这样近距离看到它们。

column5: I've only ever seen them when they wilt and fall off.\nBut being up here, and seeing them fresh? Wow...\nI wish I could take some with me, but I know I can't.
column6: 我以前只在它们枯萎飘落时见过。\n可在这里，看到它们鲜活的样子？哇……\n真希望能带一些走，但我知道不行。

column5: He runs his hands through some of the bloodleaves, clearly in awe.
column6: 他伸手拂过一些血叶，满脸惊叹。

column5: You know, this doesn't feel like I thought it would.\nI thought it'd feel amazing, like I'd become a different person.\nBut I feel just like I did before. I guess that's how things go, huh...?
column6: 你知道，这感觉和我想的不一样。\n我以为会很奇妙，像变成了另一个人。\n可我感觉和从前一样。我想事情就是这样吧……？

column5: Oh well — at least that's one more thing I can cross off my list.\nA bit anticlimactic, but I don't really know what I was expecting.\nMaybe it's like Eastcrown. Just — the allure of the unreachable.
column6: 算了——至少我又能从清单上划掉一项。\n有点虎头蛇尾，但我自己也说不清在期待什么。\n也许就像东冠一样。只是——那份遥不可及的诱惑。

column5: He inches a bit closer to me, and rests his head on my shoulder.{w}\nI can't see his face, but I can just tell that he's wearing the widest smile.
column6: 他又向我靠近了些，把头靠在我的肩上。{w}\n我看不到他的脸，但我能断定他正咧着嘴笑。

column5: You know, this is a bit different than that back alley in Mazeo.\nI'm glad that we have more privacy, and that we could do this together.\nWhen we first left Valinorth, I had no idea we'd become this close to each other.
column6: 你知道，这跟马泽奥那条后巷不太一样。\n我很高兴这里更私密，而且我们能一起做这件事。\n我们刚离开瓦利诺斯时，我完全没想到我们会变得这么亲密。

column5: Not that it's an unwelcome change. Trust me, I always thought about this.\nBut back then — a scribe-in-training dating someone like you was frowned upon.\nLook how much has changed. The entire world is nothing like we thought it was.
column6: 也不是说这变化不好。相信我，我一直都在想这件事。\n但那时候——一个见习书记官和你这样的人交往，是会遭人非议的。\n看看变化有多大。整个世界都和我们以为的截然不同。

column5: You know, I used to come to this tree, and listen for the spirits.\nI thought that if I listened closely, they might talk to me, you know...?\nBut they didn't. And now I know what that silence truly meant.
column6: 你知道，我以前常来这棵树，聆听灵的声音。\n我以为只要仔细听，它们也许会跟我说话，你懂吗……？\n但它们没有。现在我知道那份沉默真正意味着什么了。

column5: All of us were held back by The Triumvirate.\nBut now we're strong, and unified in purpose.\nI know that together, there's nothing we can't do.
column6: 我们所有人都被三人执政团束缚着。\n但现在我们变得强大，目标一致。\n我知道，只要我们同心协力，就没有做不到的事。

column5: And it's all the more special because I have you by my side.\nYou're the man that I love — and there's nothing that can change that.\nI'm following you to the ends of the world, to the highest reaches of the skies.
column6: 而因为我身边有你，这一切才更加特别。\n你是我爱的男人——没有什么能改变这一点。\n我会追随你到天涯海角，直至苍穹之巅。

column5: And it's all the more special because I have you by my side.\nYou're the woman I love — and there's nothing that can change that.\nI'm following you to the ends of the world, to the highest reaches of the skies.
column6: 而因为我身边有你，这一切才更加特别。\n你是我爱的女人——没有什么能改变这一点。\n我会追随你到天涯海角，直至苍穹之巅。

column5: And I'll have your hand the entire time...
column6: 而这一路上，我都会握着你的手……

column5: He slowly reaches down to my hand, and intertwines his fingers with mine.{w}\nThen he brings my hand up to his face, and gives the top a soft kiss.
column6: 他缓缓伸手握住我的手，与我十指相扣。{w}\n然后他把我的手举到面前，在手背上轻轻一吻。

column5: I wish this moment could last forever...\nBut that would be selfish of me. We have stuff to do.\nThankfully, we'll always have this memory. It's perfect.
column6: 真希望这一刻能永远持续下去……\n但那样就太自私了。我们还有事要做。\n幸好，我们会永远拥有这段回忆。它完美无缺。

column5: He looks around the area one last time, admiring a view he may never see again.
column6: 他最后环顾四周，欣赏着也许再也见不到的景色。

column5: Well, should we get back down to the surface?\nI don't want to waste much time up here. We're busy, and all that.\nIt means a lot to me that we could share this moment. I'll never forget it.
column6: 好吧，我们该回到地面去了吗？\n我不想在这儿浪费太多时间。我们很忙，之类的。\n能与你共享这一刻，对我意义重大。我永远不会忘记。

column5: With that, he starts to climb back down.{w}\nI follow after him, and make our way to the surface.{w}\nIt feels weird to be down here, after being so high up.
column6: 说完，他开始往下爬。{w}\n我跟着他，一路回到地面。{w}\n在那么高的地方待过之后，回到这里感觉怪怪的。

column5: So, what's next on the agenda...?\nYou know what? Never mind. You do you.\nI'll be around if you need me for any reason at all.
column6: 那么，接下来还有什么安排……？\n算了。不问了。你做你的事吧。\n如果你有任何需要，我都在。

column5: He walks away with a big smile on his face.{w}\nI guess a dream of his came true on that day.{w}\nWhen we got to Balteus, he'd have no regrets.
column6: 他脸上挂着大大的笑容走开了。{w}\n我想那天他实现了一个梦想。{w}\n等我们到巴尔泰乌斯时，他将毫无遗憾。

column5: Pro leads me to Mazeo's town square, without saying much.{w}\nI'm not sure what's going on, but he seems happier than usual.{w}\nThings must be going well for him. I hope it's something good.
column6: 普洛没多说什么，带我来到马泽奥的城镇广场。{w}\n我不确定发生了什么，但他似乎比平时更开心。{w}\n他一定是碰上好事了。希望是件好事。

column5: After a while, he rests his back against a nearby house.{w}\nTapping his foot, it looks like he's waiting for something.
column6: 过了一会儿，他把背靠在旁边的一栋房子上。{w}\n他轻点着脚尖，似乎在等什么。

column5: Okay, [firstname]. You're not going to believe this!\nI got some information about my parents the other day.\nAfter pulling a few strings, I was able to set up a meeting.
column6: 好了，[firstname]。你肯定不敢相信！\n前几天我得到了关于我父母的消息。\n托了些关系之后，我安排了一次见面。

column5: That is actually a huge deal! I'm really happy for him.
column6: 这可真是件大事！我真为他高兴。

column5: As far as I know, it's just my Dad.\nI think my Mom was under the weather or something.\nBut at this point, I'll take whatever I can get. I'm so excited...!
column6: 据我所知，只有我父亲会来。\n我想我母亲身体不太舒服之类的。\n但事到如今，能见到谁我都愿意。我太激动了……！

column5: I'll finally get to ask him what happened.\nDo you think I have any brothers or sisters?\nWait — don't answer that. I'll keep my hopes low.
column6: 我终于能问他当年发生了什么。\n你觉得我有没有兄弟姐妹？\n等等——别回答。我还是别抱太大希望。

column5: He has a huge smile on his face, and I can understand why.{w}\nThis is something he's been looking forward to for his entire life.{w}\nThe ability to meet his parents, and find out why they abandoned him.
column6: 他脸上挂着大大的笑容，我理解为什么。{w}\n这是他一生都在期盼的事。{w}\n能够见到父母，弄清他们为何抛弃他。

column5: I almost don't believe this is happening.\nFor the last decade, I've had eyes and ears everywhere.\nPeople run around Mazeo, gathering information for me to sell.
column6: 我几乎不敢相信这是真的。\n过去十年里，我到处都有眼线。\n人们在马泽奥四处奔走，为我搜集情报去贩卖。

column5: I prefer to do all the work myself, but anything extra is a huge benefit.\nI'm good at selling, so they provide the info, and then we share the profit.\nWhen we got back from Alarinthia, one of them had a bunch of stuff to share.
column6: 我更愿意凡事亲力亲为，但额外的收获也大有好处。\n我擅长兜售，所以他们提供情报，我们分成。\n我们从阿拉林西亚回来后，其中一人有一堆东西要告诉我。

column5: And one of them was the one piece of information I've been waiting to hear.\nMy parents were alive — and living in Mazeo. All those years, and they were so close.\nI bought the information from him myself. I paid more than I have for anything else in my life.
column6: 其中一条正是我一直等着听到的消息。\n我的父母还活着——而且就住在马泽奥。这么多年，他们竟离我这么近。\n我亲自从他手里买下了这条情报。我付出的价钱比我此生买任何东西都多。

column5: But you can't put a price on this kind of stuff, you know?\nMy future, and my heart is on the line. This is a {i}big{/i} deal.\nI hope we don't have to wait too much longer. I'm nervous.
column6: 但这种事是无法用价钱衡量的，你懂吗？\n我的未来、我的心都悬在这里。这可是{i}天大的{/i}事。\n希望我们不用再等太久。我好紧张。

column5: That much was made evident by his constant rambling.{w}\nI press my back against the wall with him, and we wait together.{w}\nWe talk about random subjects — anything to pass the time, for now.
column6: 他不停地絮叨，已经说明了这一点。{w}\n我和他一起靠在墙上，一起等待。{w}\n我们聊些无关紧要的话题——眼下只要能打发时间就好。

column5: But after a while, finding topics to discuss becomes a little harder.{w}\nThat's not because our bond is weak, but because we've run out of topics.{w}\nThe time of the meeting approached, and then faded away. Nobody arrived.
column6: 但过了一会儿，找话题就变得有些困难了。{w}\n并非因为我们的情谊淡了，而是话题用光了。{w}\n约定的时间临近，又悄然过去。没有人来。

column5: I guess he's running a bit late...\nIt happens. I can't hold it against him.
column6: 我想他是迟到了吧……\n这种事难免。我不能怪他。

column5: He smiles, and it's an incredibly nervous smile.{w}\nHe knows deep down inside that his words may not be true.{w}\nA couple more hours pass, but I don't abandon his side. Not even once.
column6: 他笑了，那笑容紧张得不行。{w}\n他内心深处知道，自己的话也许并不属实。{w}\n又过了几个小时，但我不曾离开他身边。一次也没有。

column5: Any moment, now...
column6: 随时都会来了……

column5: After a while, we slump down and sit on the ground.{w}\nHis naive hope starts to dissipate into a harsh realization.{w}\nBut I can tell he doesn't want to admit it. So we continue to sit.
column6: 过了一会儿，我们颓然坐到地上。{w}\n他天真的希望开始消散，化为残酷的现实。{w}\n但我看得出他不愿承认。于是我们继续坐着。

column5: As the sun sets, people start to retreat to their homes.{w}\nI can tell that he's tired, and so am I. I close my eyes for a few moments.{w}\nIt wouldn't hurt to doze off for a little bit. I just need to make sure I don't leave him.
column6: 夕阳西下，人们开始各自回家。{w}\n我看得出他累了，我也是。我闭上眼休息了片刻。{w}\n打个盹也无妨。我只需确保自己不离开他。

column5: I awaken a while later, unsure of the time.{w}\nBut it's dark — it must be the dead of night.{w}\nPro snores softly, with his head resting on my shoulder.
column6: 不知过了多久，我醒了过来，分不清时辰。{w}\n但天已经黑了——一定是深夜。{w}\n普洛轻轻打着鼾，头靠在我的肩上。

column5: I awaken a while later, unsure of the time.{w}\nBut it's dark — it must be the dead of night.{w}\nPro rests beside me, snoring softly. Asleep.
column6: 不知过了多久，我醒了过来，分不清时辰。{w}\n但天已经黑了——一定是深夜。{w}\n普洛躺在我身旁，轻轻打着鼾。睡着了。

column5: I know that in his slumber, he doesn't have to face the facts.{w}\nHis Dad never came. But why? Was he too afraid to follow through?{w}\nPro has a smile on his face. I can tell that he's still hopeful, even in sleep.
column6: 我知道，在睡梦中，他不必面对事实。{w}\n他父亲始终没来。可为什么？是他临阵退缩，不敢来了吗？{w}\n普洛脸上带着微笑。我看得出，即便在睡梦中，他依然抱有希望。

column5: But he can't sleep forever. He needs to wake up and face this.{w}\nGiving him a soft nudge, he wakes up. But then, my heart is broken.{w}\nHe thinks I woke him up because his Dad arrived. He looks around, ecstatic.
column6: 但他不能永远睡下去。他需要醒来面对现实。{w}\n我轻轻推了推他，他醒了。可随即，我的心碎了。{w}\n他以为我叫醒他是因为他父亲来了。他环顾四周，欣喜若狂。

column5: But then he realizes that it's just me and him.{w}\nHis ears fold back, and he laughs. Almost like he's not surprised.{w}\nI knew that this would be hard for him to face. But he was abandoned again.
column6: 但他随即意识到，只有我和他。{w}\n他的耳朵耷拉下来，笑了。几乎是毫不意外的样子。{w}\n我知道这会让他难以面对。可他再一次被抛弃了。

column5: I guess I should've expected this.
column6: 我想我本该料到的。

column5: He sighs, and crosses his arms.
column6: 他叹了口气，双臂交叉。

column5: You know, I thought I'd give them the option.\nThey could come meet me when they were ready and willing.\nOther than that, my only option was to just march into their home.
column6: 你知道，我本想给他们一个选择。\n等他们准备好、愿意的时候，可以来见我。\n除此之外，我唯一的选择就是直接闯进他们家。

column5: Of course my courtesy just ends up stabbing me in the back.\nHe said he'd be here, [firstname]. He said he would, and I trusted him!
column6: 结果我的体谅反倒捅了我一刀。\n他说过会来的，[firstname]。他说过会来，我信了他！

column5: He growls, and punches the nearby wall in a fit of rage.
column6: 他低吼一声，愤怒地一拳砸向旁边的墙。

column5: It's not fair...!
column6: 这不公平……！

column5: He grunts in pain, and stands there, panting.{w}\nA few tears start to stream from his eyes.
column6: 他痛得闷哼一声，站在原地喘着气。{w}\n几滴泪水开始从他眼中滑落。

column5: Why don't they love me...?
column6: 他们为什么不爱我……？

column5: I step forward, and wrap my arms around him.{w}\nHe starts crying more, and rests his head against my body.
column6: 我上前一步，张开双臂抱住他。{w}\n他哭得更厉害了，把头靠在我身上。

column5: I step forward, and place a comforting arm on his shoulder.{w}\nHe starts crying a bit more, but I let him know that I'm here for him.
column6: 我上前一步，把手搭在他肩上安慰他。{w}\n他哭得又厉害了些，但我让他知道，我陪着他。

column5: I just wanted a family...\nMore than anything, I want to belong.\nIt hurts so much that they don't want me.
column6: 我只是想要一个家……\n我最想要的，就是有个归属。\n他们不要我，这太让人伤心了。

column5: I want to know why they threw me away.\nIt's all I've ever wanted to know. That's why I do what I do.\nI don't know if I can live the rest of my life without knowing the truth.
column6: 我想知道他们为什么把我丢掉。\n这是我一直唯一想知道的。这就是我干这一行的原因。\n我不知道自己能不能在不知真相的情况下过完余生。

column5: He starts to calm down, and soon enough, the tears fade.{w}\nI can tell he's super conflicted. He really wants to meet his parents.{w}\nBut if they don't want to meet him, there's really nothing he can do.
column6: 他开始平静下来，很快，泪水也止住了。{w}\n我看得出他内心极度矛盾。他真的很想见到父母。{w}\n但如果他们不想见他，他也实在无能为力。

column5: It was cruel to schedule a meeting and then not follow through.{w}\nHis Dad must've gotten cold feet. Or maybe his Mother needed attention.{w}\n\"Under the weather\" could have any number of meanings. Not many of them good.
column6: 约好了见面却又不来，这太残忍了。{w}\n他父亲一定是临阵退缩了。又或者他母亲需要人照顾。{w}\n“身体不舒服”可以有很多种解释。多数都不太好。

column5: Either way, it's evident that this pursuit of the truth is causing him more harm than not.{w}\nIf he wasn't meant to know the truth — then perhaps he should focus on moving forward.{w}\nAfter all, he had a loving family in The Rebellion. We would never abandon him like this.
column6: 无论如何，很显然，追寻真相带给他的伤害比不去追更大。{w}\n如果他注定不该知道真相——那也许他该专注于向前看。{w}\n毕竟，他在反抗军里有爱他的家人。我们绝不会这样抛弃他。

column5: I just don't know what I should do...
column6: 我只是不知道该怎么办才好……

column5: I tell him to let go of his parents. He has a true family in all of his allies.{w}\nBlood isn't what makes you family. It's love, acceptance, and understanding.{w}\nIf his parents wouldn't give him that, then perhaps he should be abandoning them.
column6: 我告诉他，放下他的父母。他的所有战友就是他真正的家人。{w}\n血缘并不能决定谁是家人。爱、接纳与理解才能。{w}\n如果他的父母给不了这些，那也许该是他抛弃他们。

column5: Let them go...?
column6: 放下他们……？

column5: He seems surprised, like nobody has suggested this to him before.
column6: 他似乎很惊讶，仿佛从没有人向他提过这个建议。

column5: I know you're right. I've tried, but it's really hard.\nWhat happened here today might change things, though.\nAfter everything I've tried, maybe this is the wake up call I needed.
column6: 我知道你说得对。我试过，可真的很难。\n不过，今天在这里发生的事也许会改变一些东西。\n在试过一切之后，也许这正是我需要的当头棒喝。

column5: Thanks, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。

column5: I tell him not to give up. If he could gain more info, he could pursue his parents.{w}\nHe's on the right track right now, so he shouldn't give up. He's so close.{w}\nEven if it doesn't end well — at least he'd finally know the truth.
column6: 我告诉他别放弃。如果能得到更多情报，他就能去追寻父母。{w}\n他现在走对了路，所以不该放弃。他就快成功了。{w}\n就算结局不好——至少他终于能知道真相。

column5: I never even considered giving up.\nAlthough, I came close just a moment ago.\nThis \"meeting\" was definitely a wake up call.
column6: 我从没想过放弃。\n不过，就在刚才，我差点就放弃了。\n这次“见面”绝对是一记当头棒喝。

column5: If they won't come to me, then I'll go to them.\nIt might not end well, but at least I'd get some answers.\nOr maybe I can send one of my men to ask them a few questions.
column6: 如果他们不肯来见我，那我就去找他们。\n可能结局不好，但至少我能得到一些答案。\n或者，我可以派一个手下去问几个问题。

column5: Thanks, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。

column5: He smiles at me. I'm glad I could help him — even if it's only a little bit.
column6: 他朝我微笑。我很高兴能帮到他——哪怕只是一点点。

column5: So, should we get going then?\nI guess you have a lot of things to do.\nGiven that, I'm really glad that you came with me.
column6: 那么，我们该走了吗？\n我想你有很多事要忙。\n正因如此，我真的很高兴你陪我来了。

column5: I don't know how I would've handled this alone.\nHaving you by my side — it makes me stronger.\nAnd if there's anything I need right now, it's strength.
column6: 我不知道独自一人该怎么面对。\n有你在身边——让我更坚强。\n如果说我现在需要什么，那就是力量。

column5: With that, we start to walk away from the town square.{w}\nIt pained me to see him go through this. Nobody should feel abandoned.{w}\nBut at the end of the day, he had people like me to stand by his side and help.
column6: 说完，我们开始离开城镇广场。{w}\n看到他经历这些，我很心痛。谁都不该有被抛弃的感觉。{w}\n但归根结底，他还有像我这样的人站在他身边帮他。

column5: So no matter what happened — he'd never be alone.
column6: 所以无论发生什么——他都不会孤单。

column5: I stand alone in my room, swinging the blade from side to side.{w}\nEverything feels different than it did back at the start of my journey.{w}\nWhen I first touched the blade, I could barely even hold on to it.
column6: 我独自站在房间里，左右挥动着那把刃。{w}\n一切都与旅程开始时不同了。{w}\n我第一次触碰这把刃时，几乎连握都握不住。

column5: But now, I'm starting to master it. I'm able to make it my own.{w}\nHowever, just as I think that — the blade disappears from my hand.{w}\nUlric laughs, and I turn around. I didn't even notice him come in.
column6: 但现在，我开始驾驭它了。我能让它为我所用。{w}\n然而，就在我这么想时——刃从我手中消失了。{w}\n乌尔里克笑起来，我转过身。我甚至没注意到他进来。

column5: Sorry. It's just an old prank I used to pull on Sovy.\nI'd take the blade from him when he least expected it.\nI guess it has a time and place. Sorry if I startled you.
column6: 抱歉。这只是我以前常对索维使的老把戏。\n我会在他最意想不到的时候把刃拿走。\n我想这得分场合。如果我吓到你了，抱歉。

column5: He swings the blade a few times, before handing it back to me.{w}\nI shake my head. He didn't startle me. It was actually kind of funny.
column6: 他挥了几下刃，然后递还给我。{w}\n我摇摇头。他没吓到我。其实还挺好笑的。

column5: I came here because I assume you wanted answers.\nLearning I was The Grand Inquisitor must've been a shock.\nI'm glad you have a clear head. You could tell that I've changed.
column6: 我来这儿是因为我猜你想要答案。\n得知我曾是大审判官，一定让你很震惊。\n我很高兴你头脑清醒。你能看出我变了。

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点点头。

column5: But you deserve to know what I was like before I changed.\nIn order to hide from my past, I haven't exactly been honest.\nBut I wasn't lying to you. It was more like I was lying to myself.
column6: 但你应该知道我改变之前是什么样子。\n为了逃避过去，我算不上诚实。\n但我没有骗你。更像是在骗我自己。

column5: In a way, it sort of makes sense. I just decide to let him talk.{w}\nHe approaches me, and sits down on the bed. I sit beside him.
column6: 某种意义上，这说得通。我决定让他说下去。{w}\n他走近我，在床边坐下。我坐到他身旁。

column5: There was a man named Ulric in Alarinthian legend.\nHe pledged to change the nation, just like I always have.\nThe barbaric way of running things was too much for him to bear.
column6: 阿拉林西亚的传说中有个叫乌尔里克的人。\n他发誓要改变这个国家，就像我一直想做的那样。\n那野蛮的统治方式令他无法忍受。

column5: A lot of the specific details have been lost to time, but it goes like this:\nHe was young, and his parents wanted the same thing. So they fought for it.\nThey died in the arena, and Ulric couldn't handle it. He ran away from the nation.
column6: 许多具体细节已湮没于岁月，但故事是这样的：\n他年少时，他的父母也怀着同样的愿望。于是他们为之抗争。\n他们死在竞技场里，乌尔里克无法承受。他逃离了这个国家。

column5: But he pledged to return one day, and change Alarinthia for good.\nThe ideals passed on to him by his parents still live on to this day.\nThat's likely what inspired Vivien to launch his own insurrection.
column6: 但他发誓有朝一日要回来，彻底改变阿拉林西亚。\n父母传给他的理想，至今仍在延续。\n这很可能就是激励薇薇安发动叛乱的原因。

column5: Of course, the story that's handed down is never really the truth.\nTo put it bluntly — I'm the same Ulric. It's been so long, it's hard to believe.\nI'm sure you had your suspicions, so I just came here to confirm them for you.
column6: 当然，流传下来的故事从来都不是真相。\n直说吧——我就是那个乌尔里克。过了这么久，实在难以置信。\n我确信你有过怀疑，所以我来这里替你证实。

column5: It actually is a bit hard to believe, but I let him continue.
column6: 这确实有点难以置信，但我让他继续说。

column5: My parents hated the way the nation was run.\nThey passed that hatred down on to me as I grew up. But they got older.\nBefore too long, they were decrepit. They could never change anything.
column6: 我父母痛恨这个国家的统治方式。\n我成长的过程中，他们把那份憎恨传给了我。但他们也在老去。\n没过多久，他们便年老体衰。他们再也改变不了什么。

column5: So the burden was passed on to me, a rising star in the coliseum.\nI never fought for leadership. Just regular tournaments — but I never lost.\nOne day, I guess The Triumvirate noticed how strong I was. They approached me.
column6: 于是重担落到了我身上——竞技场里一颗冉冉升起的新星。\n我从不为领袖之位而战。只是参加普通比赛——但我从未输过。\n有一天，三人执政团大概是注意到了我有多强。他们找上了我。

column5: They told me that if I left Alarinthia behind, they'd train me.\nThey'd give me the power to return one day, and change everything.\nI was young and naive. I agreed without hesitation. I wanted to serve our \"Gods\".
column6: 他们告诉我，只要我抛下阿拉林西亚，他们就训练我。\n他们会赐我力量，让我有朝一日能回来，改变一切。\n我年轻又天真。毫不犹豫就答应了。我想侍奉我们的“神明”。

column5: But before they accepted me, I had to prove that I was truly ready.\nServing them would involve leaving everything behind. It'd be a fresh start.\nThey devised a test for me. To make sure that I was truly ready to devote myself.
column6: 但在接纳我之前，我必须证明自己真的准备好了。\n侍奉他们意味着抛下一切。那将是全新的开始。\n他们为我设计了一场考验。以确保我真的准备好奉献自己。

column5: They...
column6: 他们……

column5: He gulps, like he's afraid to tell me what happens next.
column6: 他咽了口唾沫，似乎不敢告诉我接下来发生了什么。

column5: They made me kill my parents.
column6: 他们逼我杀了我的父母。

column5: He looks down at the floor.
column6: 他低头看着地面。

column5: In their eyes, it told them that I was truly ready to leave my old life behind.\nBecause I was young, and stupid — it made a twisted kind of sense in my head.\nI did that they told me to. But as they died, I told them I was making their dream a reality.
column6: 在他们看来，这证明我真的准备好抛下旧日人生。\n因为我又年轻又愚蠢——这在我脑子里竟然扭曲地讲得通。\n我照他们说的做了。但在他们死去时，我告诉他们，我正在让他们的梦想成真。

column5: I was caught, and exiled into the desert. That's how I became a \"sixer\".\nI survived the trials — was branded with this tattoo — and showed my worth.\nTheir test was over. They took me over to Balteus and made me their servant.
column6: 我被抓住，流放到沙漠。我就是这样成了“六人众”的一员。\n我熬过了试炼——被烙上这个刺青——证明了自己的价值。\n他们的考验结束了。他们把我带到巴尔泰乌斯，让我做他们的仆从。

column5: I served them by weeding out insurrections and ensuring they remained in power.\nAfter what seemed like an eternity, they came up with the idea of giving me an Apprentice.\nThat's when I met Sovy. They preyed on his weakness and naivety much like they did mine.
column6: 我为他们效力，铲除叛乱，确保他们大权在握。\n在仿佛过了永恒之后，他们想出了给我派一个学徒的主意。\n我就是那时遇见索维的。他们利用他的软弱和天真，就像当初对我一样。

column5: We worked together, travelling the world, and killing The Triumvirate's enemies.\nEventually I realized that they weren't good people. I defected, and joined The Rebellion.\nIf the timeline seems confusing, it's because it is. We're talking about millennia here.
column6: 我们并肩行动，走遍世界，诛杀三人执政团的敌人。\n最终我意识到他们不是好人。我叛逃了，加入了反抗军。\n如果这时间线让人困惑，那是因为它本就如此。我们说的是数千年。

column5: He's lived for millennia...?
column6: 他活了数千年……？

column5: They gave us the \"gift\" of immortality. Well, they called it a gift.\nWe would never succumb to old age. And mortal wounds would easily fade.\nI felt unstoppable, like I was the king of the world. Nothing could get in my way.
column6: 他们赐予我们“永生”这份“礼物”。嗯，他们称它为礼物。\n我们永远不会因衰老而死。致命的伤口也会轻易愈合。\n我感觉自己势不可挡，仿佛是世界之王。没有什么能阻挡我。

column5: He shrugs, clearly embarrassed at admitting such a fact.
column6: 他耸耸肩，显然为承认这样的事实而难堪。

column5: But after a while, I realized it was a curse.\nIt's crazy how much your perspective can shift so fast.\nTaking the dream of immortality into real life — it became a nightmare.
column6: 但过了一段时间，我意识到那是个诅咒。\n人的看法竟能如此迅速地转变，真是不可思议。\n把永生的美梦带进现实——它变成了噩梦。

column5: With a slight scoff, he stands up and turns around to face me.
column6: 他轻蔑地哼了一声，站起身转过来面对我。

column5: They knew what they were doing. They were creating slaves.\nUsing that blade, they gave us what they deemed eternal life.\nI know we can use the blade, too — but we can't reverse it.
column6: 他们清楚自己在做什么。他们在制造奴隶。\n用那把刃，他们赐予我们所认为的永生。\n我知道我们也能使用那把刃——但我们无法逆转它。

column5: That should've been the first sign.\nI thought we did this willingly, but we really had no choice.\nIt was all or nothing. An ultimatum. The biggest red flag.
column6: 那本该是第一个警示。\n我以为我们是自愿的，可其实我们别无选择。\n要么全盘接受，要么一无所有。最后通牒。最大的危险信号。

column5: I've had this curse for far too long. It's made me a bad person.\nI no longer seek love, because everybody I love is just lost to time.\nI no longer seek happiness, because it's never permanent. Never.
column6: 这个诅咒缠着我太久了。它把我变成了一个坏人。\n我不再追寻爱，因为我所爱的每个人都消逝于时光。\n我不再追寻幸福，因为它从不长久。从不。

column5: These fleeting emotions may mean a lot to you — but not me.\nIt's an endless cycle of building myself up, only to be cut back down.\nI thought I'd be like this until the world rotted away. Until I met you, that is.
column6: 这些转瞬即逝的情感对你或许意义重大——但对我不是。\n这是无尽的循环：把自己建起，又被击倒。\n我以为我会这样直到世界腐朽。直到我遇见了你。

column5: He reaches out and holds my hands, squeezing them softly.
column6: 他伸出手握住我的手，轻轻捏了捏。

column5: Someone who can use the blade. Someone who can lift the curse.\nAnd — after all we've been through — even someone I can grow old with.\nPlease use that blade, and give me my life back. I don't want to belong to them.
column6: 一个能用那把刃的人。一个能解除诅咒的人。\n而且——经历了这一切之后——还是一个能与我白头偕老的人。\n请用那把刃，把我的生命还给我。我不想再属于他们。

column5: I think I want to belong to you...
column6: 我想，我愿属于你……

column5: He smiles.
column6: 他笑了。

column5: Now there's somebody else who can use the blade.\nSomebody to lift this curse, and give me my life back.\nMy life belongs to your cause, [firstname]. Not theirs.
column6: 现在有了另一个能用那把刃的人。\n一个能解除这诅咒，把我的生命还给我的人。\n我这条命属于你的事业，[firstname]。不属于他们。

column5: So please — give me that life.\nThen, after that, I can give it to you.
column6: 所以求你——把那条命给我。\n然后，在那之后，我可以把它交给你。

column5: I could remove the curse The Triumvirate put on him...?{w}\nThat would be good, but then he'd be weak and vulnerable.{w}\nNo doubt the source of his strength is partly due to his \"immortality\".
column6: 我能解除三人执政团加在他身上的诅咒……？{w}\n那固然好，但那样他会变得虚弱而脆弱。{w}\n毫无疑问，他的力量有一部分正是源自那份“永生”。

column5: If I remove it, he could perish during our attack on Balteus — and easily.{w}\nIt would be removing his biggest advantage, and I'm not sure what to do.{w}\nHe looks at me, awaiting my response. I don't know what to say next.
column6: 如果我解除它，他可能在我们进攻巴尔泰乌斯时丧命——而且是轻而易举地。{w}\n那等于夺走他最大的优势，我拿不定主意。{w}\n他看着我，等我的答复。我不知道接下来该说什么。

column5: I tell him I'll remove the curse.{w}\nHis face lights up like I've never seen before.
column6: 我告诉他，我会解除诅咒。{w}\n他的脸亮了起来，我从未见过他那样。

column5: He takes a few steps forward and plants a soft kiss on my cheek.
column6: 他上前几步，在我脸颊上轻轻一吻。

column5: Thank you so much...
column6: 太感谢你了……

column5: I grab the blade, and try to figure out what to do.{w}\nOne thing was for sure — he'd soon have his life back.{w}\nHe would have the freedom to grow old, and finally find peace.
column6: 我握起那把刃，试着弄清该怎么做。{w}\n有一点可以肯定——他很快就能取回自己的生命。{w}\n他将拥有衰老的自由，并终于得到安宁。

column5: And before he leaves my room, I make sure that his dream becomes a reality.
column6: 在他离开我房间之前，我确保他的梦想成为现实。

column5: I tell him that I can't do it, and I apologize.{w}\nGoing into Balteus, it would likely become a death sentence.{w}\nI couldn't put a friend in a situation where they'd likely lose their life.
column6: 我告诉他我做不到，并向他道歉。{w}\n进入巴尔泰乌斯，这多半会变成一道死刑判决。{w}\n我不能把朋友置于很可能丧命的境地。

column5: He crosses his arms, and I can tell that he's frustrated.
column6: 他双臂交叉，我看得出他很沮丧。

column5: You're lucky that I respect you.\nBut I'm not going to drop this — you have my word.\nThis is something I want for myself more than anything.
column6: 你很幸运，我敬重你。\n但我不会就此作罢——我向你保证。\n这是我最渴望为自己争取的东西，胜过一切。

column5: And I plan to get it, some way or another.
column6: 而我打算得到它，无论如何。

column5: With that, he walks out of the room.{w}\nEven if that didn't end well, he still opened up to me.{w}\nI know that I had his trust and respect leading into the final battle.
column6: 说完，他走出了房间。{w}\n即便结局不算好，他仍然向我敞开了心扉。{w}\n我知道，在走向最终决战之前，我拥有他的信任与敬重。

column5: But was that enough...? I guess I'd have to wait and find out.
column6: 但这就够了吗……？我想，只能等时间来揭晓。

column5: Damek leads me to the town square of Mazeo.{w}\nBecause of our recent conversations, I know what's going on.{w}\nHe's taking me to the spot where he lost his Mother during the occupation.
column6: 达梅克带我来到马泽奥的城镇广场。{w}\n因为我们近来的谈话，我知道这是怎么回事。{w}\n他要带我去占领期间他失去母亲的地方。

column5: It must be hard on him. I can see him shaking as we walk through the town.{w}\nBut if facing this painful memory helped him move on, it was my duty to assist him.{w}\nIn the coming storm, he needed to be resolute. Helping him would help all of us.
column6: 这对他来说一定很难受。穿过城镇时，我能看到他在发抖。{w}\n但如果直面这段痛苦的回忆能帮他走出来，那协助他就是我的责任。{w}\n在即将到来的风暴中，他必须坚定。帮他，就是帮我们所有人。

column5: I can't thank you enough for coming with me, [firstname].\nThere's not many people I trust this much. I'm really glad I have you.\nUntil today, I've only had dreams about doing this. But now, I'm strong enough.
column6: 你陪我一起来，我感激不尽，[firstname]。\n能让我如此信任的人不多。我真的很庆幸有你在。\n直到今天，我只能梦见做这件事。但现在，我足够坚强了。

column5: And honestly, it's all because of you.\nI give a little credit to my near-death experience, but not all of it.\nYou've grown into a capable leader, and led us all down the right path.
column6: 说实话，这都多亏了你。\n我把功劳分一点给我的濒死经历，但不是全部。\n你已成长为一个有能力的领袖，带领我们所有人走上了正确的道路。

column5: He smiles, and I smile back at him.{w}\nIt was nice to receive some support after all we've been through.{w}\nBeing the Monarch wasn't very easy. But it's a weight I had to carry.
column6: 他笑了，我也朝他笑了笑。{w}\n经历了这一切之后，能得到一些支持真好。{w}\n当君主并不轻松。但这是我必须背负的重量。

column5: We walk through the town square, taking back alleys for occasional shortcuts.{w}\nAfter a while, we end up at a large open area. I'm surprised they haven't built shops here.
column6: 我们穿过城镇广场，偶尔走后巷抄近路。{w}\n走了一阵，我们来到一片开阔的大空地。我很意外他们没在这里建商铺。

column5: This is where town meetings are held.\nThey don't happen very often, but they need a big open space.\nThere's a lot of people in Mazeo, so everyone deserves a chance to attend.
column6: 这里是举行镇民集会的地方。\n集会不常开，但需要一大片开阔场地。\n马泽奥人很多，所以每个人都该有机会参加。

column5: Soon after that, however, his tone becomes more serious.
column6: 但没过多久，他的语气变得严肃起来。

column5: A lot of bodies in one place...\nThat's just what they needed during the occupation.\nThis is where it happened, [firstname]. The stuff with my Mother.
column6: 一大堆人聚在一处……\n那正是占领期间他们所需要的。\n就是在这里发生的，[firstname]。关于我母亲的那些事。

column5: I nod at him as we take steps closer toward the center.
column6: 我们朝中心走去，我朝他点了点头。

column5: You may notice a crimson tint on the ground here.\nThis is where they piled the bodies during the attack.\nSo much blood — so much carnage. Permanently stained.
column6: 你也许注意到这里的地面透着暗红。\n袭击时他们就把尸体堆在这里。\n那么多的血——那么多的杀戮。永远地渗进了地面。

column5: Just like the memories in my head.\nAs hard as I try, I can't just scrub those off, either.\nEvery other night, I wake up in a cold sweat — crying.
column6: 就像我脑海里的记忆一样。\n无论我怎么努力，也无法把它们擦掉。\n每隔一晚，我都会一身冷汗地惊醒——哭着醒来。

column5: I feel the lingering touch of her hand against mine.\nThen, the moment she goes away, it makes me feel empty inside.\nThere's nothing to feel, except all those corpses pressed against me.
column6: 我能感觉到她的手留在我手上的余温。\n然后，在她消失的那一刻，我内心一片空虚。\n除了那些紧贴着我的尸体，什么都感觉不到。

column5: A warmth that slowly dissipates, leaving me cold and alone.\nI had to stay under them until things died down. Almost a whole day.\nThe moment I could — I got out — and took her pendent along with me.
column6: 那份温暖缓缓消散，留我独自冰冷。\n我不得不躲在它们下面，直到外面平息。几乎整整一天。\n一有机会——我就爬了出来——并带走了她的吊坠。

column5: It's all I have to remember her by. But perhaps, that's why I can't let go.\nHow can you move on from something when you remind yourself of it every day?\nJust a thought, of course. But after all I've been through, at least it's a thought with merit.
column6: 那是我纪念她的唯一物件。但也许，正因如此我才无法释怀。\n当你每天都提醒自己想起某件事时，又怎能放下它？\n当然，这只是我的想法。但经历了这一切，至少这想法有几分道理。

column5: He holds up his hand, and shows me the pendent he's holding.{w}\nI've seen that a few times, now. He seems to carry it with him everywhere.{w}\nOf course, as he suggested, that also means he carries the memory along as well.
column6: 他抬起手，让我看他手里的吊坠。{w}\n到现在，我已见过几次了。他似乎走到哪儿都带着它。{w}\n当然，正如他所说，那也意味着他同时带着那份记忆。

column5: Let's keep moving.\nI'll show you exactly where it happened.\nJust — stay close to me okay? This is hard.
column6: 我们继续走吧。\n我会带你去看它确切发生的地方。\n只是——跟紧我，好吗？这很难受。

column5: I nod, and start to follow him as we venture deeper into the open area.{w}\nA podium rests at the center. Likely where they'd hold these meetings from.{w}\nSoon, I picture what this place would look like during the occupation. I cringe.
column6: 我点点头，跟着他深入那片空地。{w}\n中央立着一座讲台。多半就是他们开会时站的地方。{w}\n很快，我想象出占领期间这里会是什么模样。我不由得缩了缩身子。

column5: After a while, Damek stops dead in his tracks, and looks down at the ground.{w}\nHis body language and reaction tells me that this is exactly where his trauma happened.{w}\nI position myself right beside him, and wait for him to speak. I couldn't rush him, now.
column6: 过了一会儿，达梅克猛地停住脚步，低头看着地面。{w}\n他的肢体语言和反应告诉我，这里正是他创伤发生的地方。{w}\n我站到他身边，等他开口。此刻我不能催他。

column5: Well, this is it...
column6: 好了，就是这里……
